respondent_comments.quote: In the tertiary care segment of hospital operations, patient volumes, revenue and activity across the board are up, and given the economic climate, this was an unexpected result. Supply chains are operating as expected: There are few, if any, impactful back orders, deliveries are consistent and fill rates are up. Employment is still in high demand, yet our institution appears to be faring well as full-time employee positions are filling without excessive recruitment. Forecast remains above average.

snapshot_notes: S&P above bear level (pro bull definition)
macro.narrative: The current macro backdrop shows robust manufacturing expansion and rising new orders, coupled with an upward‑sloping yield curve and low VIX, indicating a favorable environment for growth. For Lilly, the uptick in patient volumes in tertiary care and the expansion of new orders translate into stronger end‑market demand for its obesity and diabetes products, while the sector tilt short is offset by the unexpected volume gains. Pricing power remains mixed as coverage deals improve access but competitive pressure from Novo Nordisk erodes margins. Input costs are likely to be mitigated by the small‑molecule design of Orforglipron, and the low financing costs support continued capex investments.

implications.why: Rising ISM new orders and higher patient volumes boost demand for Lilly’s obesity and diabetes drugs.
Competitive pressure from Novo Nordisk and coverage changes reduce list price margins.
The small‑molecule Orforglipron design lowers manufacturing costs compared to peptide GLP‑1s.
Low financing costs and a favorable yield curve enable continued investment in manufacturing capacity.
An upward‑sloping yield curve still keeps borrowing rates low, allowing cheaper debt issuance.
